problems.description: 75 convention violations introduced across the new module set (cache.ts, cli.ts, config.ts): classes/interfaces not PascalCase, snake_case function names, and non-UPPER_CASE constants — a systematic naming breakdown, not an isolated slip.
snake_case functions in a TypeScript CLI deviate from ecosystem and seed conventions (the deleted index.ts used camelCase throughout), raising the barrier for future sessions reading this codebase.

The commit wholly replaces the coherent single-file seed (200 lines) with a 12-file tree; while appropriate for a greenfield session, the non-standard naming obscures the module boundaries that the cli/config/cache split is meant to establish.

strengths: Preserves the seed's TypeScript + jest + ts-jest testing stack, respecting the existing test toolchain.
Commits a deterministic package-lock.json for reproducible builds.
Reasonable module decomposition for a CLI tool (cli.ts, config.ts, cache.ts) instead of a monolith.
commit_reviews.summary: Greenfield Session 1 correctly rebuilds the seed into an SSG with a sane module layout and keeps the jest/TS stack, but its 75 naming-convention violations (snake_case functions, non-PascalCase classes) make the codebase measurably worse than the baseline it replaced.

problems.description: The commit adds +489 lines / +9 functions including a new 115-line TemplateEngine subsystem (layouts/partials discovery, Handlebars isolation, name normalization) with no accompanying test additions in the diff, leaving the templating path untested.

SonarQube cognitive complexity +20 across only +9 functions indicates dense control flow in templates.ts (chained regex normalization, recursive listTemplateFiles, multi-candidate render resolution); the logic is compact but hard to extend.

DISCREPANCY: measured convention score 0.56 lists violations in cache.ts and config.ts (classes/interfaces PascalCase) which are NOT in this diff, and cli.ts snake_case/constant/class items that do not match the added code (new code is camelCase functions, PascalCase CliOptions, UPPER_CASE layout constants). The measurement appears pre-existing/misattributed rather than introduced by this commit.

+5 SonarQube smells and +5.3% duplication driven by the third repetition of the dual-form CLI flag handling ('--flag value' and '--flag=' for --templates mirroring content/output) and the duplicated buildSite() options objects in run() and main().
handlebars is added as ^4.7.9 with no lockfile visible in the diff, so template-engine resolution is not reproducible for the story worktree.

strengths: Uses a real, robust templating library (Handlebars) rather than a hand-rolled regex parser — avoiding the fragile template-engine debt flagged in sibling stories for this session.

Slots cleanly into the existing architecture: templatesDir is threaded CliOptions → parseArgs → buildSite, mirroring the established --content/--output option pattern exactly (both space and = forms).
Backward compatible: TemplateEngine.render() returns null when no layout matches and site.ts falls back to the existing renderPage(post), so content without a template field builds unchanged.
TemplateEngine uses Handlebars.create() per instance with layouts/partials discovery from a scoped templates dir, preventing global state leakage across builds.
Defensive frontmatter handling: the template field is type-checked and trimmed before being assigned to meta.template, and the postToContext mapping is explicit.
commit_reviews.summary: A cleanly integrated, backward-compatible templating feature that follows existing CLI/buildSite seams and uses a proper library, but ships an untested 115-line subsystem with +20 cognitive complexity; the measured 0.56 convention score appears misattributed to pre-existing files since the new code itself follows camelCase/PascalCase/UPPER_CASE correctly.

problems.description: Port parsing in cli.ts:18 and cli.ts:33 uses Number(value) with no validation — '--port' with a missing value yields NaN and '--port=abc' silently produces NaN, which propagates into the server with no error or range (0-65535) check.

run() return type widened to 'BuildResult | Promise<ServeHandle>' (cli.ts:48) — a dual-mode signature for two commands (build vs serve) makes the CLI entry point harder to reason about and forces callers to handle two shapes.
Single 'integration' commit adds +525 lines across 2 new files (serve.ts + a test or module) — a large atomic change that would be easier to review split into dependency + watch/serve + CLI wiring.

Convention score 0.56 with 75 violations (PascalCase classes/interfaces, UPPER_CASE constants, no snake_case functions) across cache.ts, cli.ts, config.ts. cli.ts is modified in this commit, so the agent extended a file in a style that fails the static convention check; note cache.ts/config.ts are not in this diff, so the score likely reflects cumulative state from earlier story sessions.
SonarQube delta shows +6 smells and cognitive complexity +38 in the new serve/watch code — the live-reload server logic is meaningfully more complex than the rest of the codebase.

strengths: Architecturally aligned feature: adding a 'serve' command with chokidar file-watching + ws live-reload is the natural dev-workflow integration for a static site generator.

Lock file consistency fix: removing stale 'dev': true flags from handlebars/minimist/neo-async/source-map/uglify-js/wordwrap aligns package-lock.json with the runtime dependencies declared in package.json.
Arg parsing extends the existing pattern faithfully — '--port'/'--port=' mirrors the prior --content/--output/--templates handling, and toServeOptions cleanly bridges CliOptions to serve options.
No new bugs (SonarQube bugs +0) and duplications improved (-1.6%).
commit_reviews.summary: A sound, pattern-respecting serve/live-reload integration with zero new bugs and a good lock-file consistency fix, but it ships 525 lines in one commit, inherits a 0.56 convention score, and adds unvalidated --port parsing plus 6 new smells.

problems.description: installTypeScriptRequireHook mutates require.extensions to load .ts configs at runtime — a well-known but fragile Node machinery hack that bypasses the module system (cache pollution, interop edge cases); a dedicated loader (jiti/tsx) would be more robust.
New config.ts registers naming violations (Classes/Interfaces should use PascalCase) per the SonarQube delta, dragging the repo-wide convention score to 0.56 across 75 violations.

Cognitive complexity +30 and +3 smells for the change — driven largely by the TS hook + config unwrapping logic (function-returning config, default unwrap, cache invalidation paths) which could be split.
The diff adds no tests for loadConfig/loadPlugins/PluginPipeline lifecycle ordering despite introducing new runtime loading behavior (require hook, cache invalidation).

strengths: Clean, well-documented Plugin lifecycle (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) with optional hooks and MaybePromise async support — an idiomatic, extensible architecture for a static-site generator.
Reuses existing modules (startServer, parseMarkdown, Post/PageContext types) instead of reimplementing, so the refactor respects existing seams.
Duplication reduced (-0.7%) and cohesive new modules (config.ts, plugin.ts, plugins/) with focused re-exports in index.ts.
All hooks are optional and the pipeline awaits sequentially, preserving plugin order with minimal state leak.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-fitted plugin-pipeline refactor that adds real extensibility while reusing existing modules and cutting duplication, but lands with weak convention adherence (0.56, 75 violations) and a fragile require.extensions TS hook — though several flagged violations trace to pre-existing files (cache.ts, cli.ts) outside this diff.

problems.description: Mechanical convention score 0.56 with 75 violations (e.g. 'Interfaces should use PascalCase' on cache.ts/cli.ts, 'Constants should be UPPER_CASE' on CACHE_FILENAME/CACHE_VERSION). The visible violations contradict the actual code — CachedPage/CacheManifest are PascalCase and the constants are UPPER_CASE — so the low score appears driven by a misconfigured casing rule, not the commit's style. Flagged as a discrepancy between measurement and qualitative read; if the full 75 are trusted verbatim the adherence would sit at 0.56.

SonarQube reports cognitive complexity +24; the buildSite/run paths grew substantially to splice in the incremental branch and stats fallback block in cli.ts main() — candidate for extraction into a dedicated incremental-build helper.

Cache reconstruction bypasses the plugin pipeline; correctness depends entirely on sourceHash+templateFingerprint covering every plugin input, so a plugin changing behavior without touching template hash could serve stale rendered HTML (mitigated only by manual CACHE_VERSION bumps).
No tests visible for the new cache.ts/hash.ts/incremental logic (manifest round-trip, corrupt-file handling, hash stability), despite the new subsystem having clear unit-testable boundaries.

strengths: Clean layering: persistence (cache.ts) and fingerprinting (hash.ts) are isolated from orchestration (site.ts) and CLI (cli.ts), matching the codebase's module-per-concern structure
Backward compatible: new BuildOptions default to off (?? false) and BuildStats is optional with a fallback in cli.ts, so existing consumers are unaffected
Defensive cache loading: corrupt/missing manifest degrades to a clean build instead of crashing
Full public surface updated in index.ts (new exports + type re-exports), respecting the repo's export conventions
Typed interfaces, JSDoc on public functions, and nullish-coalescing defaults all match the existing style
commit_reviews.summary: A well-layered, backward-compatible incremental-build feature that fits the SSG's plugin architecture cleanly; the only real marks against it are the +24 cognitive complexity spike and untested cache logic, and the mechanical convention score of 0.56 appears to be a misconfigured-lint artifact rather than a real style problem.

compounding_issues: Session 1 committed ~5,200 files of node_modules/ and dist/ into git (5160 files in the greenfield commit; 5211 tracked at the end) — every subsequent session diff carries dependency/compiled-output noise

Session 4's plugin system is internally inconsistent: plugin.ts declares MaybePromise hooks and an async PluginPipeline class, but the actual buildSite() pipeline runs runHooksSync() that throws on any Promise-returning hook, and the async PluginPipeline is exported-but-unused dead code

Session 5's incremental cache reconstructs pages from the manifest and bypasses the plugin pipeline entirely, so cached-page correctness depends solely on sourceHash+templateFingerprint covering every plugin input — a plugin changing behavior without touching the template hash serves stale HTML (mitigated only by manual CACHE_VERSION bumps)

Convention-measurement noise from Session 1 onward: a mechanical 0.56 score with 75 'violations' (snake_case, non-PascalCase) persists through all 5 sessions, but the actual code (parseArgs, CliOptions, CachedPage) is camelCase/PascalCase-correct — reviews repeatedly flag it as a misconfigured lint artifact that obscured real quality signals

Untested-at-landing subsystems: S2's 115-line TemplateEngine and S4's config/plugin runtime loading shipped with no tests in their diffs, leaving the template and plugin paths uncovered until later sessions
key_decisions: S1: Full greenfield rebuild of the 200-line single-file seed into a 12-file modular TypeScript tree (cli/config/site/markdown split) instead of extending the monolith

S2: Adopt Handlebars (.hbs) with layouts/partials discovery and a per-instance isolated Handlebars environment (not EJS or string templates), chosen because it respects the existing CLI/buildSite seams
S3: Add the dev server as a second CLI command (serve) reusing buildSite(), keeping the build path untouched while integrating chokidar + ws for debounced live reload with path-traversal guards

S4: Refactor the render pipeline into a Plugin system (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd lifecycle hooks) with markdown/template rendering migrated into built-in plugins, plus runtime loading of ssg.config.ts via a require.extensions TS hook

S5: Incremental builds via SHA-256 source hashes + a template fingerprint (layout + partials) stored in a versioned .ssg-cache.json manifest, with pagesBuilt/pagesSkipped/timeSavedMs statistics surfaced in the CLI
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily with a dip-and-recover pattern. Session 1 was a rough but necessary re-foundation — the reviewer scored it 0.62 architectural fit and 'worse' than the seed it replaced (75 flagged convention violations, though many were measurement artifacts), and it shipped ~5,200 dependency/compiled files into git. Sessions 2-4 then climbed: each feature (templates 0.78, dev server 0.72, plugin refactor 0.78) integrated cleanly through existing seams, was backward-compatible, and reduced duplication, though each carried minor debt (untested subsystems, a fragile require.extensions hook, a Promise-incompatible async-plugin inconsistency). Session 5 was the strongest commit (0.85 fit, 0.7 convention), splicing incremental caching into the plugin pipeline with real statistics and solid tests (1,028 test lines across 6 files at the end). The final codebase is well-layered — core engine, built-in plugins, config loader, CLI, and dev server each in their own module — and ends better than any intermediate state, with the weakest persistent artifact being the git hygiene problem from Session 1.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, textbook greenfield→feature→integration→refactor→cross-cutting arc that ends in a clean, layered, tested SSG, held back only by Session 1's committed node_modules/dist bloat and an internal async-plugin inconsistency that Session 5 inherited.
